'''Terry Quinn''' [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] is a British [[physicist]] and was director of the [[International Bureau of Weights and Measures]] from 1978 to 2003.<ref name="MartinMetrologia2003">{{cite journal |last=Martin |first=P. W. |title=The end of an era |journal=Metrologia |volume=40 |issue=6 |article-number=E01 |date=2003-12-01 |url=https://doi.org/10.1088/0026-1394/40/6/E01|doi=10.1088/0026-1394/40/6/E01 |access-date=2026-09-15}}</ref>

== Education ==
'''Terry Quinn''' graduated in physics from [[University of Southampton]] in 1959 and then moved to Oxford for his PhD in what was then the Metallurgy Department under the supervision of Prof. [[William Hume-Rothery]].<ref name="QuinnNewcomen2024">{{cite web |title='Measuring the Metre' by Dr Terry Quinn FRS |url=https://www.newcomen.com/activity/measuring-the-metre-by-dr-terry-quinn-frs/ |website=The Newcomen Society |publisher=Newcomen – London Branch |date=2024-10-09 |access-date=2026-09-15}}</ref> In 1962, he joined the [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|National Physical Laboratory]] in Teddington as a junior research fellow where he worked on radiation thermometry, temperature scales, and acoustic determination of the gas constant.<ref name="Colclough1979">{{cite journal |last1=Colclough |first1=A. R. |last2=Quinn |first2=T. J. |last3=Chandler |first3=T. R. D. |date=September 1979 |title=An acoustic redetermination of the gas constant |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences |volume=368 |issue=1732 |pages=125–139 |doi=10.1098/rspa.1979.0119 |bibcode=1979RSPSA.368..125C |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rspa/article/368/1732/125/14875/An-acoustic-redetermination-of-the-gas-constant |access-date=12 September 2026|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== BIPM ==
Dr. Quinn joined the BIPM as physicien chercheur principal on September 1977, to take up the position of Deputy Director starting on 1978.<ref>{{cite book |author=[[International Committee for Weights and Measures|Comité International des Poids et Mesures]] |title=Procès-Verbaux des séances |volume=Tome 45 |series=2e Série |date=1977 |publisher=Bureau International des Poids et Mesures |location=Sèvres, France |isbn=92-822-2049-4 |language=fr |url=https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/17315032/CIPM66.pdf |access-date=2026-09-12}}</ref> During this time he developed further interest in mass and balances resulting in a new determination of [[gravitational constant]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Quinn |first=Terry |date=2000-12-21 |title=Measuring big G |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=408 |issue=6815 |pages=919–920 |doi=10.1038/35050187 |pmid=11140663 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35050187 |access-date=2026-09-12|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Quinn |first1=T. J. |last2=Speake |first2=C. C. |last3=Richman |first3=S. J. |last4=Davis |first4=R. S. |last5=Picard |first5=A. |date=2001-08-27 |title=A New Determination of G Using Two Methods |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume=87 |issue=11 |article-number=111101 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.111101 |pmid=11531510 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..87k1101Q |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.111101 |access-date=2026-09-12}}</ref>

While at the BIPM he also continued collaboration in work at NPL on the development of the cryogenic radiometer, a method now universally employed for measuring electromagnetic radiation, and which led to determinations of the Stefan-Boltzmann constant.<ref name="QuinnMartin1984">{{cite journal |last1=Quinn |first1=T. J. |last2=Martin |first2=J. E. |title=Radiometric Measurements of the Stefan-Boltzmann Constant and Thermodynamic Temperature between -40 °C and +100 °C |journal=Metrologia |volume=20 |issue=4 |pages=163 |date=1984 |url = https://doi.org/10.1088/0026-1394/20/4/005 |doi=10.1088/0026-1394/20/4/005 |access-date=2026-09-15}}</ref> From 1984 to 1985 he was a Lady Margaret Distinguished Visiting Fellow at the Cavendish Laboratory,
Cambridge, where he worked on the anelastic properties of a Cu-Be alloy used in flexure strip balances.<ref name="QuinnSpeakeDavis1986">{{cite journal |last1=Quinn |first1=T. J. |last2=Speake |first2=C. C. |last3=Davis |first3=R. S. |title=A 1 kg Mass Comparator Using Flexure-Strip Suspensions: Preliminary Results |journal=Metrologia |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=87 |date=1986 |url=https://doi.org/10.1088/0026-1394/23/2/002 |doi=10.1088/0026-1394/23/2/002 |bibcode=1986Metro..23...87Q |access-date=2026-09-15}}</ref>

Dr. Quinn became director of BIPM on 1 August 1988 on the retirement of Prof. Giacomo. As director of the BIPM, Dr. Quinn has greatly increased international recognition of the importance of the role of accurate measurement in today's world. In 2002, he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society and retired from the BIPM on 31 December 2003.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr Terence Quinn CBE FRS |website=The Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/william-thomson-12129/ |access-date=2026-09-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Martin |first=P. W. |date=2002 |title=Dr Terry Quinn, Director of the BIPM, elected a Fellow of the Royal Society |journal=[[Metrologia]] |volume=39 |issue=2 |pages=125 |doi=10.1088/0026-1394/39/2/1 |bibcode=2002Metro..39..125M |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0026-1394/39/2/1 |access-date=2026-09-12|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Dr. Quinn is a Fellow of the Institute of Physics (UK), a Fellow of American Physical Society and of the American Association for the Advancement of Science. Dr. Quinn was made a Commander of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) by the Queen in the 2004 New Year Honours list.<ref name="TheTimesDiplomatic2003">{{cite news |title=Diplomatic and Overseas List |url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/advice/diplomatic-and-overseas-list-qlmdg639s07 |work=[[The Times]] |date=2003-12-31 |access-date=2026-09-15}}</ref>
